/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 10 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3521 (-99)
Baltic Capesize Index: 6122 (-278)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2409 (-5)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1713 (9)
Baltic Handysize Index: 931 (9)
CAPESIZE
There was a noticeable shift in sentiment today, with the market giving back some of its recent gains as weaker offers emerged across both basins. The BCI 182 5TC fell $2,522 to $55,519, while the C5 index declined 0.850 to $17.885 and C3 eased 0.191 to $41.727. The Pacific weakened, with three C5 miners in the market but offers noticeably lower from the outset, with $18.50 initially on offer. One miner set the tone by fixing at $17.75, followed by two further fixtures reportedly concluded below $18. Following the recent uptick in C3 activity, sentiment also softened, with bids harder to come by while offers remained in the $42.00-$42.50 range. The Atlantic similarly lost ground, with pressure emerging on both South Brazil and West Africa to China business, while the North Atlantic also came under strain. A softer transatlantic fixture emerged, contributing to C8 falling $3,075 to $55,938.
PANAMAX
The P5TC eased by $41 to $21,684, highlighting the largely flat sentiment across both basins. Despite the slight decline, Fronthaul activity continues to show signs of strength, with market participants reporting increased demand for both mineral and grain cargoes, particularly within specific laycans where vessel availability remains tight. Trading activity has been somewhat subdued today due to the Geneva holiday, with several market participants using the opportunity to assess the market's direction. In the Trans-Atlantic sector, market sources highlighted that vessel supply remains plentiful from the North Continent, placing pressure on rates. However, sources have also stated there have been indications of tightening conditions in the Western Mediterranean, which could provide support to sentiment in the region. Coal exports from Indonesia into India are reported by market participants to remain healthy, encouraging charterers to reassess their rate ideas in an effort to attract owners away from alternative re-positioning destinations such as South China. Longer Pacific round trips are also said to be gaining momentum, with offers moving above recent levels as demand continues to strengthen. This is helping to underpin overall market fundamentals and providing further support to sentiment across the basin.
SUPRAMAX
Despite a holiday in Geneva sentiment remained positive as a whole, with the 11TC average rising $118 to close at $21,655. In Asia the market appeared to be flat except trips to East coast India/Bangladesh which are now having to pay slightly higher levels to attract Owners, but otherwise very little movement or reports surfaced. The Esper (55,848 2012) prompt Hong Kong was reported fixed for a trip to Port Louis intention cement at $22,000 with Hanson, however a source claimed this had been concluded last Friday at something around $19,000, but unfortunately it was not possible to clarify the correct level. The Atlantic seemed quieter due to the holiday with few notable trades being rumoured, but the Arabella (63,619 2015) Port Harcourt 14-16 September was taken by Reachy basis delivery Santos for grains to China at $19,500 plus $950,000 ballast bonus, although another source had heard the level to be $18,500 plus $850,000 ballast bonus, but neither rate could be confirmed.
HANDYSIZE
The Handy market saw another mixed day, with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. The BHSI closed at 931, while the 7TC average increased by $148 to finish at $16,751. The Continent and Mediterranean remained steady with very limited fixing activity and flat sentiment prevailing. In contrast, activity in the US Gulf remained healthy, supported by a balanced tonnage list and strong underlying demand. The Federica (36,612 2012) was reported placed on subjects for a trip from Mobile to the Ushant–Skaw range with wood pellets at $19,000 by NYK. The South Atlantic appeared sideways, with the bid-offer gap remaining wide and rates largely flat and the AB Bonita (33,811 2011) Douala 25-30 Sep was reportedly fixed on voyage basis Upriver to SE Asia at an equivalent of about $14,500 from Douala, but further details were lacking. The Pacific market appeared balanced, although a slight increase in tonnage was noted in Southeast Asia, prompting participants to adopt a cautious wait-and-see approach with the Locomotion (38,046 2013) Penang said to have fixed in the $18,000s for an Australian round voyage, but there were no further details.

Market Fundamentals
Russian Grain Exports

Agricultural consultancy Sovecon, lowered its Russian total grain and pulse export forecast for MY 2026/27 by 4.4 Mt from the August to 49.4 Mt. The 2026/27 wheat export forecast was also lowered 3.2 Mt to 41.4 Mt, as the Black and Azov Sea continued to face disruptions to shipments, newswires report. Shipments have been redirected through land and rail, Baltic ports and the Caspian Sea but at severely reduced volumes. Sovecon expects wheat exports in September to stand at 2.0 Mt, down slightly from 2.2 Mt in their previous forecast, and normalisation not on the horizon at least until late-Autumn according to the report.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape market pushed lower today, with the main activity concentrated in September, October and Q4. September opened around 53,000 before easing to 52,500 and then trading mainly around 51,800–52,000 through the rest of the session, with a late print at 51,800. October started around 49,000, traded as high as 49,250, but spent most of the day around 48,500–48,850 and finished near 48,800. November traded between 45,500–45,900, while December was around 43,500. Q4 remained close to 46,000 for most of the session, with a late dip to 45,950 before returning to 46,000. Q1 27 traded largely around 31,400–31,500, while Cal 27 was around 34,000–34,100.

PMX
PMX was softer overall today. September traded around 22,100 early, dipped to 22,000 through the morning, and later returned to 22,100. October opened around 23,750, briefly reached 23,850, then softened to 23,500–23,600 where later activity was concentrated. November traded around 23,150 early before easing through 23,000 to 22,900–22,950 later on. December moved from 22,000 down to around 21,825–21,900. Q4 opened around 23,000 before steadily easing to 22,800, where strong volume traded through the afternoon. Q1 27 also weakened from 18,700 early to 18,500 late, while Q2 27 traded around 19,600.
